pages.lr-26677:
Benjamin Conde

U.S. SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION

Litigation Release No. 26677 / October 21, 2026

Securities and Exchange Commission v. Benjamin Conde, et al., No. 19-cv-05404 (E.D.N.Y. filed Sept. 23, 2019)

SEC Files Proposed Final Judgment Against Defendant Charged in Alleged Penny Stock Manipulation Scheme

On October 20, 2026, the Securities and Exchange Commission filed a proposed final judgment against Benjamin Conde in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York in connection with an alleged fraudulent scheme to manipulate the market for the securities of Renewable Energy and Power, Inc. ("RBNW").

According to the SEC's complaint, filed on September 23, 2019, Conde orchestrated a scheme between March and July 2017 to manipulate the market price and trading volume of RBNW securities. The complaint alleged that Conde acquired millions of shares of RBNW, funded and coordinated a promotional campaign through a boiler room operation, and engaged in matched and wash trading designed to create the false appearance of active trading and artificially inflate the stock price. The complaint further alleged that Conde profited from the scheme by selling shares into the manipulated market at artificially high prices, causing substantial losses to retail investors.

In a parallel criminal action, Conde pleaded guilty to, among other charges, conspiracy to commit securities fraud.

Conde consented to the entry of a final judgment, subject to court approval, that would permanently enjoin him from violating the antifraud provisions of Section 17(a)(1) and (3) of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rules 10b-5(a) and (c) thereunder, as well as the market manipulation provisions of Section 9(a)(1) of the Exchange Act; impose a penny stock bar; and order Conde to pay disgorgement of $1,097,800 and prejudgment interest of $1,681,021.69, for a total of $2,778,821.69, which would be deemed satisfied by the restitution and forfeiture orders entered against him in the parallel criminal case. The final judgment against Conde, and the Commission’s voluntary dismissal of its claims against Relief Defendants Essex Global Investment Corp. and Facultas Capital Management, Inc., concludes the litigation.

The SEC's investigation was conducted by Andrew Elliott and Cecilia Connor. The litigation was handled by James E. Smith and Matthew F. Scarlato and supervised by James Carlson. The SEC appreciates the assistance of the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority.
pages.lr-26676:
Siddhi Patel, as Administrator of the Estate of Chirayu Vijay Patel (Deceased)

U.S. SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION

Litigation Release No. 26676  / October 20, 2026

Securities and Exchange Commission v. Siddhi Patel, as Administrator of the Estate of Chirayu Vijay Patel (Deceased), No. 2:26-cv-13587 (D.N.J. filed Oct. 19, 2026)

SEC Files Settled Action Against the Estate of Fund Manager who Allegedly Defrauded Over 40 Investors

On October 19, 2026, the Securities and Exchange Commission filed settled charges against the estate of Chirayu Vijay Patel, alleging that Patel misled over 40 investors about the performance and security of their investments and misappropriated investor funds for his own personal expenses.  

According to the SEC’s complaint, Patel solicited investments in two offerings, one in which Patel promised investors fixed returns of 6% per year, and the other in which he described as having a higher risk-return profile and target returns of 20% per year.  The complaint alleges that between around July 2020 and November 2025, Patel pooled together approximately $10 million that he obtained from investors through the offerings, misappropriated approximately $1.2 million for personal expenses, returned approximately $1.5 million to some investors through Ponzi-like payments, and lost over $7 million through trading.  The complaint further alleges that Patel repeatedly provided investors with false and misleading account statements and false rates of return, leading them to believe that he was generating profits when in fact he had lost or misappropriated nearly all of their money.

The SEC’s complaint, filed in U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey, charges Patel with violating the antifraud provisions of Section 17(a) of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5 thereunder.  Without admitting the allegations in the SEC’s complaint, the administrator of Patel’s estate consented to the entry of a final judgment, subject to court approval, which would order the estate to pay disgorgement of $1,204,597.77 plus prejudgment interest of $198,497.46. 

The SEC's investigation was conducted by Michael C. Ellis and James Flynn, and supervised by Lindsay S. Moilanen and Sheldon Pollock, all of the SEC's New York Regional Office.  The litigation will be led by Christopher Colorado.
pages.lr-26675:
Terrance P. Berland and David Michael Scalzo

U.S. SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION

Litigation Release No. 26675 / October 20, 2026

Securities and Exchange Commission v. Terrance P. Berland and David Michael Scalzo, No. 26-cv-02430 (M.D. Fla. filed Oct. 19, 2026) 

SEC Files Settled Action Against a Former Officer and a Former Director of a Florida Photonics Company

On October 19, 2026, the Securities and Exchange Commission filed settled charges against Terrance P. Berland, former CEO and minority owner of Violet Defense Group, Inc., a now defunct Florida photonics company, and David Michael Scalzo, its former director and majority owner, in connection with their alleged misrepresentations concerning the company’s projected revenues for 2021 and use of investor funds.

According to the SEC’s complaint, filed in U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida, from at least April 2021 through November 2021, Berland and Scalzo raised approximately $13 million from 88 investors through a securities offering in the form of Class B shares in Violet Defense Group. As alleged, Berland and Scalzo negligently misrepresented that the company was on track to reach $15 million to $18 million in revenues in 2021 and that 10% of the funds raised from investors would be used for marketing and branding for its largest subsidiary, and, in securities purchase agreements disseminated to investors between August and October 2021, Berland and Scalzo gave false assurances that nothing had occurred that could reasonably be expected to result in a material adverse effect on the company’s financial condition.  As alleged, Berland and Scalzo should have known by August 2021 – but failed to disclose or correct – that these financial projections were inaccurate because the company’s sales and royalty revenues had declined significantly, and by the end of August 2021, that more than 40% of investor funds were committed to a NASCAR team sponsorship. 

Without admitting the allegations in the complaint, the Defendants have consented to the entry of final judgments, subject to court approval, which would permanently enjoin them from violating Section 17(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933, and order each to pay a civil penalty of $100,000.   

The SEC’s investigation was conducted by Brian Theophilus James, with assistance from Lina M. Fernandez and Brian Lechich, and supervised by Thierry Olivier Desmet and Stephanie N. Moot of the SEC’s Miami Regional Office.
pages.lr-26674:
Nihat Cardak

U.S. SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION

Litigation Release No. 26674 / October 19, 2026

Securities and Exchange Commission v. Robert Bernardi, Nihat Cardak, and Sunil Chandra, Defendants, and Daniel Bernardi, Diane Olson, and Jenifer Bernardi, Relief Defendants, No. 21-cv-08598 (S.D.N.Y. filed Oct. 20, 2021)

SEC Settles Litigation with Former CFO of Software Company Charged with Multimillion Dollar Fraud 

On October 16, 2026, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filed a consent and proposed final judgment as to Nihat Cardak, former CFO of GigaMedia Access Corporation (Giga), a private software company, in the SEC’s civil enforcement action against him.

The SEC’s complaint, filed on October 20, 2021 in United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, alleged that, between March 2018 and August 2019, Cardak and the former CEO of Giga raised more than $37 million from investors while repeatedly misrepresenting the company’s financial condition. 

Cardak consented to the entry of a final judgment, subject to court approval, that would permanently enjoin him from violating Section 17(a) of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5 thereunder; and order him liable for disgorgement in the amount of $210,400 with prejudgment interest of $17,231.02, which amounts shall be deemed satisfied by the order of restitution entered against him in a parallel criminal case, United States v. Nihat Cardak, No. 21 CR 616 (PGG) (SDNY). 

The SEC’s litigation was conducted by Melissa Armstrong, David Nasse, and Kristen Warden, with the assistance of Ashley Dolan Barrachina, of the SEC’s Home Office.
